$comment: Origin allow-list cases for the WebSocket acceptor (spec/transports/websocket.md, Origin). verdict: accept | reject. origin is absent when the upgrade carried no Origin header. allowed is the acceptor's configured list.

cases.name: y_absent_origin_is_not_a_browser
cases.$comment: No Origin means no browser attached one; the credential check governs such a dialler, not this list.

cases.name: n_empty_allow_list_refuses_every_origin
cases.$comment: An acceptor that serves only native clients configures nothing and refuses every browser.

cases.name: n_suffix_is_not_a_match
cases.$comment: A suffix or endsWith comparison would admit any domain the attacker registers under.

cases.name: n_port_must_match
cases.$comment: A different port is a different origin; the default port is never implied.

cases.name: n_trailing_slash_is_not_an_origin
cases.$comment: A serialised origin has no path, so a value carrying one never matches.

cases.name: n_null_is_a_value_not_an_absence
cases.$comment: Browsers send the literal null for a sandboxed or file origin; it is admitted only when listed.

cases.name: n_wildcard_is_not_special
cases.$comment: There is no wildcard in this comparison; a list entry is one exact origin.

cases.name: n_case_differs
cases.$comment: A browser lowercases the scheme and host it sends; anything else did not come from one.
